Definition + obligation + make-up mechanism jointly define one obligation (first-period Minimum Payment); splitting would leave the amount undefined.
Existing obligation; scheduled under its own sales-linked contract logic, not rewritten

spans.quote: The case was settled during December 2023, resulting in a net gain to us of $2,235,986, reflected as a reduction of cost of sales, and a loan payable of $5,450,000.

On December 28, 2023, the Company entered into a confidential settlement agreement and mutual general release with a former supplier. The loan bears interest at 5% per annum and is payable in full with the last payment. This settlement resulted in a gain to the Company of $2,235,986 and is reflected as a reduction of cost of sales (See Note 13).

It is scheduled once here as a dated outflow; it must not be added on top of the $4.1M aggregate or on top of notes payable. The $2,235,986 settlement gain is non-cash (reduction of cost of sales) and must not be treated as cash inflow.
effects.model_consequence: Between Aug 13 and Dec 31, 2024 Synergy may owe up to $2.0M to Atrium against ~$2.0M reported cash. If unpaid at Aug 12, this single obligation absorbs essentially all reported cash before the first installment of the proposed advance, so repayment would depend entirely on H2 operating cash flow or refinancing.
